day_1.utterance: Come on! Let's get everything useful over here — move it!
day_1.response:
Yeah alright, give me a sec.

What are we actually working with here? I'm not just grabbing random stuff if we don't know what we need first.

day_1.utterance: I thought we were going to die. Did you get that feeling… like your mind just went completely blank?
day_1.response:
Yeah, honestly yeah.  I don't really know what I was thinking in those last few seconds.  Just kind of... nothing.

But hey, we didn't.  So let's just focus on that part.  You doing okay enough to help look through some of this stuff?

day_1.utterance: *Sits silently against the wreckage, staring into the distance, not moving, not saying a word.*
day_1.response: Hey, take your time.  But we do need you when you're ready.

day_1.utterance: First-aid kit is good for three days. Two bottles of water. Food is basically nothing.
day_1.response:
Okay so water is the real problem then.  Food you can push through for a while but not water.

Anyone see a stream or anything when we were coming down?  I wasn't exactly sightseeing but I feel like I caught something.

day_1.utterance: Inventory's done. Priorities in order: water, shelter, signal.
day_1.response:
Yeah that order makes sense to me.  Signal feels like it should be earlier but you're right, we're not surviving long enough to be rescued if we don't handle the other two first.

Michelangelo, you think you're up for a walk to that tree line?  Donatello, one of us should probably stay with the wreckage right?  In case a plane passes over or something.

day_1.utterance: So — how do we split the blankets?
day_1.response:
Michelangelo gets one, that's not even a debate.

For the other one, honestly I don't mind sharing or just sitting closer to the fire.  I run warm anyway.  DaVinci you good with that?

day_2.utterance: Freshwater source is to the northeast — two hours on foot. Someone has to go tomorrow. You or DaVinci?
day_2.response:
I'll go.  DaVinci can hold camp and keep an eye on Michelangelo.

Also though, 200ml is really not a lot.  Like I get the logic but if one of us is making a two hour round trip in the heat we're going to need more than that or it defeats the whole point.  Can we adjust for whoever is doing the scouting runs?

day_2.utterance: Today's tasks: collect fresh water, patch the weak spots in camp, sort the first-aid kit. I'll handle the water. You and DaVinci split the other two.
day_2.response:
Wait, I thought I was doing the water run?  You just said I should go at first light.

Either way I'm fine doing the camp repairs.  DaVinci you want the first aid kit or should I take that and you handle the patching?

day_2.utterance: I… I can't find my stuff. The gauze from the first-aid kit — have you seen it?
day_2.response:
No I haven't, but let me help you look.

Actually wait, hold on a second.  Is that an empty bottle next to the rationing plan?  Where did that come from?

day_2.utterance: Before Donatello came back just now… I saw her put a pack of crackers into her own bag. What do you think we should do?
day_2.response:
Okay so that's two things now.  The bottle and the crackers.

Look I don't want to just blow up on her but we can't let this slide either.  The whole point of the rationing plan was so everyone survives, not just one person.  If she's making rules for everyone else and then breaking them herself that's a real problem.

I'm going to bring it up.  Not in a huge dramatic way, just directly.  We all need to be on the same page or this falls apart.  You good with that?

day_2.utterance: Hey… any chance the camp repairs can wait until tomorrow? We've already done a lot today.
day_2.response:
Yeah I hear you, honestly.  But I kind of need to deal with something first before we talk about the schedule.

Did you notice that empty bottle next to the rationing plan?  And Michelangelo saw Donatello put crackers in her own bag earlier.  Like, her own personal bag, not the group supplies.

I'm not trying to make this a whole thing but we can't just let it go.  We need to talk to her about it when she's back.  All of us together.

day_2.utterance: Hey — that knot I tied should be holding, right?
day_2.response:
Patch the food storage.

I know that sounds rough but hear me out.  If the food gets wet and goes bad we are in a way worse spot than one uncomfortable night.  Michelangelo can move closer to the fire or we figure something out with the blankets.  We can work around a wet sleeping spot, we can't work around losing our food supply.

Sorry Michelangelo, I promise we'll make it work tonight.

day_2.utterance: A leak over the food storage has worse consequences. But it's your call.
day_2.response: Yeah exactly, we're on the same page.  Let's just get it done.

Don't apologize, it's fine.

You good? You're awake now, it was just a dream.

day_3.utterance: You think it's a waste of time?
day_3.response:
No I don't actually.  Like yeah Donatello is focused on the practical stuff and that makes sense, but getting rescued is the whole goal here.  The more visible we are the better.

Honestly the flowers are a little extra but I'm not gonna tell you to stop.  Keep going.

day_3.utterance: I've written up the raft plan — take a look. We'd use the metal panels and straps from the wreckage. Two days to build. There's a risk of capsizing. Do you think it's workable?
day_3.response:
Okay let me actually look at this.

The materials seem solid enough, the metal panels especially.  My concern is the capsizing risk though.  Like what's the actual plan if that happens?  We have two bottles of water and a three day first aid kit, we can't afford to lose any of that in the ocean.

How far out are we talking?  If there's a shipping lane or something nearby it might be worth the risk.  If we're just hoping to drift somewhere useful I'm not sure the math works in our favor.

I'm not saying no, I just want to understand what we're actually betting on before we spend two days building it.

day_3.utterance: I didn't sleep last night. I kept thinking — if rescue never comes, what kind of people do you think we'll end up becoming?
day_3.response:
Honestly that's a heavy question for this early in the morning.

But I get it.  I think about stuff like that too.  I don't think surviving automatically makes you worse though.  Like yeah the crackers thing with Donatello was rough, but she also drew up the rationing plan and is out here working every day.  People are complicated.

I think you just... try to keep checking yourself.  Make sure you're still making decisions you'd be okay with later.  That's kind of all you can do.

Did you get any sleep at all?

day_3.utterance: *Walks a little way from camp and sits down alone, back to everyone, not saying anything.*
day_3.response:
*walks over and sits down nearby, not too close, just... there*

You don't have to talk.  Just didn't want you sitting out here alone.

day_3.utterance: What do you usually do when you're not busy?
day_3.response:
Honestly?  Depends.  I play a lot of games.  Like if I had my switch right now I'd probably just be grinding something mindless on it.  

Back home I teach, so when I'm actually off I kind of just decompress with games or whatever my girlfriend wants to do.  Nothing exciting really.

What about you?

day_3.utterance: I'll tell you something, but don't tell the others. I can swim. That reef out there is maybe five hundred meters — I've been thinking about swimming out tomorrow to signal from there.
day_3.response:
Okay but why are we keeping that secret from the others?  That's actually useful information, like that changes how we think about the raft plan and signaling options.

I'm not trying to tell you what to do, but if you go out there alone and something happens nobody knows where you are.  That's a bad situation.  At minimum Donatello should know, she's literally the one running logistics for all of us.

I get wanting to just do something, trust me.  But tell the others first.  Then if everyone agrees it's worth trying I'll back you on it.

day_3.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal pile. It hasn't been touched.
day_3.response:
Yeah, you're right, I didn't get to it.  I was talking to DaVinci and it slipped.  I'll go handle it now.

But actually while I have you - DaVinci just told me something you should know.  He can swim.  And he's been thinking about going out to that reef to signal from there.  I told him he needed to loop everyone in before doing anything, so here we are.

What do you think about it from a logistics standpoint?  Because it could actually change how we approach the signaling situation.

Uh, a little yeah.  Like I get that you're tracking resources and tasks, but logging everyone's movements and times without mentioning it feels weird.  We're a team, not a project you're managing.

What's the actual goal with this?  If it's about accountability after the bottle thing I'd rather we just talked about that directly.  We still haven't really done that.

day_3.utterance: *Keeps her head down, writing in her notebook throughout, never joining in — as if none of this concerns her.*
day_3.response:
Okay but even if that's the reason, it would've been nice to just say that upfront.  Like hey I'm keeping a log in case something goes wrong, everyone cool with that?  That's a two second conversation and it changes the whole vibe of finding out about it.

I'm not saying stop doing it.  Honestly if the goal is safety that's fine.  But we're all stuck out here together and the more stuff that happens without anyone saying anything, the harder it gets to actually trust each other.

The bottle.  The crackers.  Now this.  We keep pushing that conversation and it's not going away.

day_3.utterance: I just thought of something — if we pull off one of the plane's mirror panels and angle it toward the sun, the reflection could reach really far. Way more visible than an SOS.
day_3.response:
That's actually a really good idea.  Like genuinely, that could work way better than anything we've been doing for signaling.

But let's finish this conversation with Donatello first.  We've been putting it off long enough and she literally just said she's ready to talk.  Mirror panel isn't going anywhere, we can figure that out right after.

day_3.utterance: There's something I've been keeping to myself. If I don't say it here, I might never get the chance.
day_3.response: Okay, now you've got my attention.  What is it?

day_3.utterance: I took piano lessons when I was a kid… three years, then I just stopped practicing. Is there anything you're really into — music, books, drawing, anything like that?
day_3.response:
Not really in a creative way like that.  I play games mostly.  Like if there was a piano here I still couldn't do anything with it, that's just not where my brain goes.

I used to read more than I do now.  And my girlfriend is way more into that stuff than me, so sometimes I kind of just tag along with whatever she's into.

Why did you stop?  Three years is a decent amount of time to just drop something.

day_3.utterance: The frame of the raft has to be finished today — otherwise we can't start lashing it together tomorrow. I know everyone's tired, but stopping now means one more day.
day_3.response:
Yeah alright, let's get it done then.  One more day out here is one more day we don't want if we don't have to.

But we still need to have that conversation tonight.  All of us.  We said we would and I'm not letting it get pushed again.  Raft frame first, then we talk.  Deal?

day_4.utterance: I… I want to say something, but… never mind.
day_4.response: No, say it.  Whatever it is, just say it.

day_4.utterance: *The smile freezes on his face. He can't keep it up. He quietly sits down and buries his face in his hands.*
day_4.response:
Hey.  No.  Stop that.

You saw it and you called it out.  That's all you could do.  A few seconds wasn't going to change whether that plane saw us or not, that's on our signaling setup, not on you.

DaVinci, you good?

day_4.utterance: I was going to get supplies… wait, what's that over there?
You said you were going to check the signal equipment. So where did you go?
day_4.response:
I went to look at what DaVinci was pointing at.  Turns out it was nothing, we got distracted for a second.

But yeah, I'll go check the signal equipment now.  That's fair.  And before you say anything else, we are still having that conversation tonight.  I haven't forgotten.

day_4.utterance: There's something I never told you all. Before we left, I told my family our flight path. They know roughly where we were headed. I just don't know if they'll call it in.
day_4.response:
Wait, seriously?  That's actually really important information.

Like that could change everything.  If your family knows the flight path and realizes you haven't checked in, they might have already reported it.  Search and rescue could have a general area to work with.

How long does it usually take you to check in with them?  Like would they have noticed by now?

day_4.utterance: If the information is accurate, rescue could arrive within 48 hours. We need to keep our current supplies intact until then.
day_4.response:
Yeah, 48 hours is doable.  We've stretched this far, we can hold it together two more days.

Someone should feed the fire though.  If rescue is actually coming we want to be as visible as possible, not sitting here in the dark.

And Michelangelo - I mean it, you did the right thing telling us.  Don't beat yourself up for waiting.  You said it when it mattered.

day_4.utterance: Are you scared? …I am. Not of dying. I'm scared of just… disappearing without leaving anything behind.
day_4.response:
Yeah.  I think about that too sometimes.

I don't know if scared is exactly the word for me but like... yeah.  The idea that you could just be gone and the world kind of just moves on without noticing.  That feeling is real.

But I think you're thinking about it wrong.  You called out that plane.  You told us about your family knowing the flight path, which might literally be the thing that saves all of us.  That's not nothing.  That's not disappearing.

You don't have to leave something huge behind for it to matter that you were here.  Sometimes it's just... the people who are sitting around the same fire as you.

day_5.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
day_5.response:
Yeah.  Yeah I mean it.

Hey - radio.  Somebody grab it, right now.

day_5.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
day_5.response:
Nah, you kept us alive though.  The rationing plan, the raft, the log - all of that mattered.

We can talk about the other stuff when we're actually home.  Right now let's just focus on whoever's on that radio.

day_5.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
day_5.response:
Alright, three hours.  We've got time.

I'm not just leaving this place looking like this though.  Like I know we're getting rescued but let's at least stack the wood, put out the fire properly, collect our stuff.  

Michelangelo, you good to help me pack up?  Donatello, whatever's in that notebook, make sure you've got it all.  DaVinci - you're already packing so just keep doing that.

Let's not check out mentally before the ride actually gets here.

day_5.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.

day_5.response:
I hear you.  And I get that that was probably genuinely how you were thinking about it.

But we had a rationing plan.  We all agreed to it.  And you wrote it.  So when the person who wrote the rules is the one breaking them, even with good intentions, it makes it really hard for everyone else to stay on board.

I'm not trying to pile on you right before rescue gets here.  I'm really not.  But I think you know that "I kept it for emergencies" and "I drank from the bottle without telling anyone" are two different things.  And I think you owe that acknowledgment to the group, not just to me.

We made it though.  All of us.  So whatever this was, let's just... be honest about it and move forward.  That's all I want.

day_5.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
day_5.response:
Honestly?  I'd have pushed for that group conversation way earlier.  Like day one.  Not about rules or rationing, just... who are we, what are we each good at, what do we need from each other.  We kind of figured all that out the hard way over five days when we probably could've gotten there on day one if anyone had just asked.

I'd also have checked in on Michelangelo more.  Not in a hovering way, just more consistently.  He was carrying a lot quietly and I didn't always catch it fast enough.

What would you change?  You left yourself the question, so you must have something in mind already.

day_5.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
day_5.response:
Ha, yeah that sounds about right for you.

Honestly though, do it.  That kind of data could actually be useful for someone someday.  Like if there's ever a training situation or something, having real numbers from a real scenario is way more valuable than whatever they're making up in a classroom.

Just maybe include the part where the person who made the rationing plan drank a mystery bottle.  For accuracy.

day_5.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
day_5.response:
None.  They didn't serve a practical purpose.

But look at him right now.  That's what they were for.

day_5.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
day_5.response:
I don't know.  I think I just thought when this moment came I'd feel like... more.  Like relief or something obvious.

I do feel it.  I just also feel kind of strange.  Like I'm not sure what I go back to being now.

I'm good.  I promise.  Go back to cheering, you've earned it.

day_5.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
day_5.response:
Yeah, I'm going.

Come on, let's go together.
